one_line_contribution: It defines the responsibility of an individual retrieved experience-memory item for an ALFWorld failure by seed-replicated re-runs with that item removed (12 seeds, two blocks, plus an emptied-set arm), and then scores cheap attribution proxies -- the agent's self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain, position prior, semantic overlap, single-seed leave-one-out, Shapley -- as a paired gap to a measured ceiling, the accuracy a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate attains against the same label. The genuinely new pieces are the unit (memory item rather than step, agent, document or set), the treatment of sampling noise as the estimand rather than a nuisance (seeds-to-label curve, split-half reliability, replicate-as-ceiling), and the attributability rate itself as a headline number.
closest_prior_work: VERIFIED, arXiv:2608.20627, 'When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic RAG' (2026-08-20; confirmed by s2cli paper and returned by two independent queries). It is already an interventional benchmark for causal failure attribution: it injects a certified fault at a specified hop, re-executes the downstream trajectory, and scores post-hoc diagnosers against the known fault, reporting 'broad evidence of post-hoc signal loss'. That is structurally E2 plus the headline framing of this proposal -- planted ground truth by re-execution, cheap diagnosers measured against it, and the finding that post-hoc attribution loses the signal. It does not sink the proposal outright: its unit is a retrieval hop in single-shot-answer agentic RAG rather than one of k co-retrieved experience items; its ground truth is injected, so it has no analogue of the natural-failure label, the attributability rate (P4), or the duplication/joint-responsibility arm (P5a); and it does not treat stochastic re-execution or the number of seeds as an estimand at all. The second threat is CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467, verified with s2cli paper: 'a lightweight intervention-based framework for measuring per-evidence-item operational utility in single-shot RAG'), whose REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE per-item intervention protocol is exactly the manipulation set here, one step short of the multi-step stochastic setting; the proposal's REMOVE-vs-token-matched-REPLACE ablation and its duplicated-culprit composition are CUE-R's perturbations transplanted. Third, arXiv:2507.04480 (verified: 'Source Attribution in RAG', PKDD/ECML Workshops, 7 citations) already asks how well SHAP approximations mirror exact document attributions while minimising LLM calls -- i.e. the accuracy-versus-cost frontier, in single-shot RAG. Net: the mechanism, the ground-truth protocol and the cost-frontier framing all exist; what is new is the unit and the noise treatment. That is a real but incremental combination, not a new question.
strongest_objection: The headline claim is measured on a population selected to make it true, and that population is a small minority of the failures the paper says systems act on. Every method-versus-ceiling comparison (P1, P2, P3, P5b, P7) is scored only on 'attributable natural episodes' -- episodes the 12-seed rule certified as having one item with r_i >= about 0.33. By the proposal's own P4 that is at most 45% of memory-caused failures, which are themselves a fraction of the roughly 240 failures, leaving 60-110 episodes (the pre-registered extension guarantees only 80). So the result reads: on the roughly 8% of episodes where a single item has a huge, seed-stable effect, cheap proxies lag intervention. But a memory system that reinforces or demotes items on failure must decide on every failure, including the majority the benchmark declares unlabelable, and on those the benchmark supplies no target for any method -- so the number the paper produces does not answer the question the paper opens with. Compounding this, at n = 80 the paired accuracy CI is +/- 11.5 points while the falsifying margins are 15-25 points, so only enormous effects are decidable and the interesting negative (a proxy that matches intervention) cannot be certified either. Second-order but damaging in review: the entailment check's two near-entailments are real and both violate the brief's own 'no prediction entailed by a definition' rule. P6 scores 'reader 2 succeeds at base' as disagreement on episodes selected because reader 1 failed, so a plain base-rate gap between backbones produces the predicted 20 points with no failure of attribution transfer whatsoever; and P3a, with ties counted as abstention, has an arithmetic single-seed ceiling near p_culprit x (1 - p(S))^2, so '< 65%' is close to guaranteed by the scoring rule rather than by the science. P5b's falsifier sits 2 points above the nominal 10% false-positive rate with per-cell interaction SE around 0.35, which is not a test. Of seven predictions, one is the load-bearing open one (P1), one is the honest risky one (P2), and three are compromised.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, roughly in order of value. (1) Make the estimand the whole memory-caused failure population, not the attributable subset: release the full r_i vector per episode and score every method by rank correlation (or top-1-with-abstention calibrated against the released r_i distribution) over all failures, with the 'no single item is responsible' outcome as a first-class label rather than an exclusion criterion. That removes the winner's-curse selection, makes P4 a statement about the world rather than about the rule's 0.79 power, and roughly triples the usable n. (2) Audit the scorers the field actually deploys. The brief's Q1 names MemQ-style Q-values over a provenance DAG, RoMeRL-style utility coordinates, usage-decay survival and admission scores; the proposal scores none of them and instead evaluates self-report, confidence gain, position and lexical overlap. As written the paper cannot say anything about the memory systems it motivates itself with. (3) Repair P6 by conditioning: make the primary estimand label transfer on the subset where reader 2 also fails at base, and report the base-rate mismatch as a separate descriptive quantity. Repair P3a by pre-registering the falsifier as a fraction of the analytic single-seed ceiling computed from the E0 p(S), or by making the random tie-break primary. Replace P5b's significance count with the pooled interaction magnitude and its CI. (4) Re-run and re-position the collision check against arXiv:2608.20627, and state explicitly what the item-level, natural-failure, seed-replicated design buys over injected hop-level faults -- the paper needs that paragraph in the introduction, not in a rebuttal.
missing_baseline: A third-party LLM diagnoser: give an off-the-shelf model the failed trajectory, the task, and the k retrieved items, and ask it to name the culprit or abstain. This is the standard attribution baseline in every paper the proposal cites as related work (A2P arXiv:2509.10401, ErrorProbe arXiv:2604.17658, CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338, the Who&When line, and the diagnosers scored in arXiv:2608.20627), it costs one call, and it is categorically different from the agent's own post-episode self-report, which is the only LLM-based method in E3. A reviewer will note that the proposal's own related-work section defines the field by these methods and then omits them from the comparison. Two cheaper omissions matter too: the retriever's own relevance score as a zero-cost ranking (the proposal has position and semantic overlap but not the score the retrieval system already computed, which is the first thing any practitioner would try), and at least one learned utility score from the brief's Q1 families. Note also that the proposal's static-procedure arm (E4) is a manipulation, not an attribution baseline, so it does not fill this hole.
preprint_collision: Not a verified collision on the central claim, but the check is materially incomplete and its closing sentence is wrong. The proposal asserts 'no preprint provides item-level responsibility labels with seed replication, a seeds-to-label curve, or an accuracy-cost frontier of attribution methods' after four queries, all in memory-item vocabulary, and it missed the nearest neighbour. Queries I ran, all answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels ok; WebSearch was unavailable this session and was not used): (1) mechanism, --recent, 'attribute agent failure to a specific retrieved memory item counterfactual removal intervention ground truth' -> arXiv:2607.13083, 2607.10608, 2608.00017, 2604.17658, 2604.05467, 2603.00026, 2509.23735, 2509.10401 -- overlaps the proposal's own list, nothing item-level with intervention labels. (2) mechanism, 'interventional benchmark injected fault re-execution evaluate failure diagnosers agentic retrieval' -> arXiv:2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP, 2026-08-20), plus arXiv:2607.11098 (AgentCheck, replay with injected faults), arXiv:2604.22708 (TraceElephant), arXiv:2603.25001, arXiv:2607.28802. 2608.20627 is the one that matters and the proposal does not cite it, though the automated novelty card surfaced it at sim 0.50; I verified it with 's2cli paper 2608.20627'. It already builds an interventional benchmark that injects a certified fault, re-executes, and scores post-hoc diagnosers against the known ground truth, reporting post-hoc signal loss -- so the proposal's E2 arm and its 'cheap attributions are much worse than intervention' framing are no longer new in kind, only in unit and in the seed-replication treatment. (3) closest named method, 'Shapley value attribution of retrieved documents source attribution RAG evidence utility' -> arXiv:2507.04480 verified (S2 metadata: PKDD/ECML Workshops, 7 citations; the s2cli 'paper' lookup on that id returned not-found, the search channel resolved it), plus arXiv:2512.05958 (MaxShapley, fair context attribution in generative search at 9x lower cost, 4 citations) which the proposal does not cite and which is a direct precedent for its accuracy-versus-cost frontier. (4) home vocabulary, 'variance and sample cost of leave-one-out data valuation noisy stochastic utility Monte Carlo Shapley replicates' -> only classical Data Shapley (1904.02868), shapiq, OddSHAP; nothing on stochastic-environment replication, so the noise angle is genuinely open. (5) 'leave-one-out removal of individual experience memory item agent success rate seeds variance' --recent -> nothing on item removal, but arXiv:2602.07150 ('On Randomness in Agentic Evals') already establishes that single-run agentic estimates carry large variance and need multiple runs, which pre-empts part of the seeds motivation at the eval level. (6) home literature on self-report faithfulness for retrieved items -> only citation-faithfulness work (2509.21557, 2510.17853, 2601.10700); the specific gap the proposal claims (self-reported memory use never tested against counterfactual re-runs) survives. Verified ids: 2608.20627, 2604.05467, 2507.04480, 2511.20857, 2602.16313 (61 cit), 2605.25338, 2509.10401, 2604.17658, 2509.23735, 2607.10608 -- all returned by the command with matching titles. Could not verify: 2605.18565, 2604.20006, 2507.05257, 2509.12765, 2401.07927, 2307.08678, 2311.07466, 2602.02639; none of these carry the novelty argument, so the failure is not load-bearing. Verdict on the check itself: honest about channels and specific about what it found, but it searched only its own vocabulary, and the paper closest to its design was one query away.
